extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, policymakers, and media/tech industry professionals interested in Japan's news ecosystem
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level profile summarising audience behaviour, market metrics, technology adoption, regulatory developments, and business-model challenges for news media in Japan. Useful for comparing national news-homepage strategies and market conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper circulation (print) and trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan's historically high newspaper circulation continued to decline to a total of 28.5 million in March 2024, down by 7.31% from the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a measure of print resilience and the pace of decline; the text links the decline to rising input costs (paper and ink) driven by a weak yen and to the sector's struggle to replace print revenues via digital business models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital subscription performance and strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Nikkei recently reached 1 million digital subscribers; Asahi Shimbun has achieved around 300,000 digital subscribers over a similar period; Yomiuri maintains strategy of only allowing digital access to print subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates success of pay/digital transition strategies. Examples of product approaches include Nikkei Prime (specialist premium content) and Minutes by Nikkei (concise briefings aimed at young readers). Guidance implies publishers should consider premium vertical content and concise formats to attract subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for online news (share of population)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple penetration metric for consumer willingness to pay; informs viability of subscription-first homepage strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to podcast in the last month: 26%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of audio/audience engagement channels relevant to news providers and homepages promoting audio content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news (national level and brand trends)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news overall: 43% (noted as =15/47). Overall trust levels remain stable, while scores for individual news brands declined by between 2 and 6 percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess credibility environment; the page points to high-profile reporting failures (e.g., delayed investigations into Johnny Kitagawa) as drivers of brand-level trust declines, suggesting reputational risk is a key homepage consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom ranking and score
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: 70/180. Score 62.12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External comparative metric for press freedoms which may affect editorial independence and regulatory constraints faced by news organisations and their homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on portals and aggregators for online news
rubrics_metrics.description: Online news is mainly accessed via free portals and aggregators such as Yahoo! and Line News. Over half (53%) cite Yahoo! News as their main source of online news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures distribution dependency. For homepage strategy, high portal/aggregator reliance implies importance of syndication relationships and indirect audience acquisition channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform economics and publisher remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Report shows publishers receive 124 yen (less than US$1) per 1,000 page views (PVs), less than a quarter (24%) of the ad revenue earned by the portals. Japan’s FTC warned that portals might breach Anti‑Monopoly Law if rates are too low and urged disclosure of how licence fees and advertising arrangements are decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates fairness/transparency in platform-publisher arrangements; suggests negotiating power, transparent pricing, and regulatory scrutiny are important considerations for publishers monetising homepages and content on platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public broadcaster remit and regulatory changes (NHK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the Broadcasting Act (tabled March 2024) aim to change NHK's internet remit from 'complementary business to broadcasting' to 'essential business', covering streaming and catch-up TV; receiving fee was cut by 10% from 2023. New services will require 'public interest tests'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the legal/regulatory scope of public service media in the digital age and potential competitive/crowding effects on commercial broadcasters and news homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming adoption and VOD/catch-up service performance
rubrics_metrics.description: More than half of households (52.7%) subscribe to at least one TV streaming service; majority use YouTube. TVer (a free catch-up VOD service by commercial broadcasters) is increasing viewing figures but is not yet consistently profitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures audience migration to on-demand video and the commercial viability of catch-up services; relevant for news homepages hosting or promoting video streams and VOD.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI adoption in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK introduced an AI newsreader in 2018 ('News Yomiko'); commercial broadcasters have followed to cut production costs. Nikkei uses AI to help summarise corporate results, but deeper analysis is still done by humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes boundaries of AI use: efficiency/automation (cost-cutting, summarisation) versus human-led deeper analysis. Relevant to homepage content generation, moderation, and trust considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinformation incidence and provenance/verification technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a major earthquake, false claims went viral (including fake rescue requests and conspiracy claims); LINE Yahoo deleted over 1,800 posts. To meet disinformation challenges, news media, advertising agencies, and platforms developed technology (digital watermark/originator profile) to identify and verify content source; Originator Profile Collaborative Innovation Partnership aims to be in use by 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures prevalence and response to misinformation and the development of provenance tools. For homepages, indicates importance of verification, moderation, and provenance metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience demographics shaping distribution choices
rubrics_metrics.description: In Japan's ageing society, over-65s make up almost a third (29%) of the population; older people still cling to TV and print, while younger groups mainly get news from online aggregators and social/video networks such as YouTube and Line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides segmentation and product decisions for homepages — e.g., designing different entry points/formats for older (print/TV-focused) vs younger (aggregator/social) audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic pressures on print supply chain
rubrics_metrics.description: With the Japanese yen at weak levels, prices of paper and ink made from mostly imported materials have hit the sector hard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A macroeconomic constraint impacting cost structures of print publishers; relevant when evaluating legacy homepage revenue models tied to print economics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product innovation targeted at younger readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include 'Minutes by Nikkei', launched in November 2023, aimed at briefing young readers in a concise way, and Nikkei Prime, a new premium service with specialist content on technology, automobiles, and green business transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates content-format and product strategies (concise briefings, vertical premium content) intended to attract younger audiences and corporate subscribers; relevant to homepage content architecture and subscription funnels.
